correctness.rationale: The Poisson series leads exactly to a real reciprocal quartic analytic-derivative numerator. A Joukowski quadratic with explicit discriminant and endpoint signs gives all interior zeros and their multiplicities. The unique double critical point and nonzero square-root coefficient follow by Taylor expansion. The standalone checker verifies the rational numerator identity and five representative parameter configurations; it is not used to prove universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The natural three-electrode Poisson problem admits a complete interior saddle count and a universal collision parameter independent of arc width. The transition from nonreal conjugate points to two real diametral equilibria has a sharp square-root law; it is a motivated global phase diagram, not a routine isolated calculation.
